assertMatrix.comment: Quality gates that every key route must clear.

Content routes are light; hold them to the full >=0.9 budget. Invisible Maps of Religion and Maps That Age join the list here rather than arriving with exceptions of their own. Both carried scholarly plates at archival size - the 2,350,999-byte Hereford mappa mundi, the heaviest committed image in the project, plus 579,360 for Matthew Paris and 981,271 and 350,421 for the two Ortelius impressions - and neither route appeared in collect.url, so those bytes were real and unmeasured at the same time. Both sliders now request display derivatives out of images/<essay>/display/, which is what lets the routes enter the list at the same 1,250,000 every other content route holds instead of raising a ceiling to meet them. The canonical plates are unchanged on disk and still served from the collection catalogue, which is where a reader who wants the archival pixels goes.

The atlas hosts an intentional heavy interactive WebGL map (MapLibre, ~800 KiB) above the fold. Its performance score and total-blocking-time are both dominated by that widget and swing by more than 2x with the machine: measured 2844ms and 2896ms on main and 2605ms on the KAN-405-414 branch on one development host, against 1238ms for the same branch on a GitHub runner. A hard TBT threshold therefore measures the runner rather than the diff - it passed on PR #117 and failed on PR #118 while the shipped JS grew by 1.8 KiB (0.14%). Both are monitored warns. The budgets that do track what this project controls - total bytes and script size - stay hard errors, as do accessibility, best-practices and SEO above.
